site.name: Universal Wisdom Library
site.tagline: A shared reading room for the world's sacred and philosophical texts
site.description: A searchable, comparative library of primary texts, translations, commentary and thematic connections across traditions. This build catalogues the complete Tanakh, Mishnah, Talmud, Midrash and Tosefta and the Halakhah, Kabbalah, Liturgy, Jewish Thought, Chasidut, Musar, Responsa, Second Temple and Reference shelves, alongside the complete Qur’an, Dhammapada and the Dīgha and Majjhima Nikāyas, and a Christian shelf of the Bible, the church fathers, the apostolic fathers, Augustine, Aquinas, Dionysius the Areopagite, Anselm, the Cloud of Unknowing, the Imitation of Christ and non-canonical Christian literature, an Islamic shelf that now includes the Sufi poets and prose writers alongside kalam, falsafa and the Arabic fiqh, hadith and tafsir works from OpenITI, a Hindu shelf of the Gita, the principal Upanishads, the Yoga Sutras, the Brahma Sutras, the Sarva-Darsana-Samgraha, the Ramayana, the Laws of Manu, the Sankhya Aphorisms and the Hatha Yoga Pradipika and the Satapatha Brahmana, a Zoroastrian shelf of the Vendidad, Yasna, Yashts and the five Pahlavi volumes, and a Buddhist shelf that now includes the Vinaya, the Jataka, the Udāna, the Therīgāthā, Aśvaghoṣa's Life of the Buddha, the Bodhicaryāvatāra, the Lotus Sutra, the Buddhist Mahayana Texts, the Questions of King Milinda and the Sutta-Nipata, and a Daoist shelf of the complete Daodejing in Wang Bi's Chinese beside Legge's English, with the Zhuangzi, the Liezi, the shorter classics and the morality books, and a Shinto shelf of the complete Kojiki in Chamberlain's 1882 translation and the thirty books of the Nihongi in Aston's 1896 translation. Texts are read from the project that hosts them rather than copied here.
site.corpusNotice: Every text names the edition, source and rights recorded by its provider. The Jewish shelves, the Pali suttas, the Qur’an, the hadith collections, the Dhammapada, the Christian Bible, the patristic and scholastic works, the apostolic fathers, the Dionysian corpus, the medieval contemplatives, the non-canonical Christian texts, the Sufi, kalam, falsafa and fiqh works, the Arabic manuals, hadith, kalam and tafsir from OpenITI, the Gita, the Upanishads, the Yoga Sutras, the Brahma Sutras, the Sarva-Darsana-Samgraha, the Ramayana, the Rigveda, the Samaveda, the White and Black Yajurveda, the Atharvaveda and the Vedic Hymns, the Laws of Manu and the dharmasastras, the Grihya Sutras, the Sankhya Aphorisms and the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, the Satapatha Brahmana, the Zhuangzi, the Liezi, the Yang Chu book, the Daoist morality books, the Canon of Reason and Virtue, Balfour's Taoist Texts, the Sayings of Lao Tzŭ and the two appendix scriptures of Legge's second Taoist volume, the Vendidad, Yasna and Yashts, the five Pahlavi volumes, the Vinaya Texts, the Jataka, the Udāna, the Therīgāthā, the Buddhacarita, the Bodhicaryāvatāra, the Lotus Sutra, the Buddhist Mahayana Texts, the Questions of King Milinda, the Sutta-Nipata, the Apostolic Fathers, Dionysius the Areopagite, Anselm, the Cloud of Unknowing and the Imitation of Christ are read from Sefaria, SuttaCentral, AlQuran Cloud, the Hadith API, the Bolls Bible API, the Christian Classics Ethereal Library, New Advent, Wikisource, Project Gutenberg, OpenITI and the Internet Sacred Text Archive when you open them: this library stores their catalogue records, chapter outlines and passage indexes, not copies of the text. Only a handful of editorial and Project Gutenberg excerpts remain local — among them the complete Daodejing, in Wang Bi's Chinese and Legge's English — together with the complete Guru Granth Sahib, whose Gurmukhi and English editions are held locally under written permission.

traditions.name: Judaism
traditions.description: The Hebrew Bible (Tanakh) and the interpretive traditions that grew around it, including Mishnah, Talmud, Midrash, Tosefta, liturgy and philosophy.
traditions.permissions_note: Texts are imported as display copies from Sefaria. The exact edition, source and licence are recorded for every version; the library does not relicense them.

traditions.name: Christianity
traditions.description: The Greek Scriptures, the Septuagint and Hebrew Bible as received in Christian communities, together with patristic, medieval and modern interpretation.
traditions.permissions_note: The King James Version and the Greek text used here are public domain. Modern translations are not included.

traditions.name: Islam
traditions.description: The Qur'an, the hadith collections and the traditions of tafsir, law, theology and mysticism.
traditions.permissions_note: The Arabic Qur'an text is reproduced verbatim under the Tanzil text terms (CC BY 3.0, no modification). Rodwell's 1861 translation is public domain. Modern translations are not included.

traditions.name: Hindu traditions
traditions.description: A family of traditions encompassing Vedic literature, the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita, epic and puranic literature, and diverse philosophical schools.
traditions.permissions_note: Sanskrit texts are streamed from GRETIL and, for the Bhagavad Gita, from the Gita Supersite at Heritage IIT Kanpur, which also supplies the Sanskrit commentaries read beside it. Nineteenth- and early twentieth-century English translations come from Project Gutenberg, the Internet Sacred Text Archive and Wikisource, each named with its translator. GRETIL's files are mostly CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the Heritage commentaries are Tier B of HCAL 1.1: both are displayed with attribution and not relicensed.

traditions.name: Buddhism
traditions.description: The Buddha's discourses and disciplinary literature in Pali and other canonical languages, with commentarial and later Mahayana and Vajrayana traditions.
traditions.permissions_note: The Pali root text is public domain; Bhikkhu Sujato's English translation is released CC0 by SuttaCentral. Attribution is retained in the edition record.

traditions.name: Sikhism
traditions.description: The Guru Granth Sahib and the writings of the Sikh Gurus, together with the Khalsa tradition and its history.
traditions.permissions_note: Catalogue entry only in this build. No English edition has been imported because the available translations require permission. The Gurmukhi text is not reproduced until its edition and licensing are reviewed.

traditions.name: Taoism and Chinese traditions
traditions.description: The Daodejing, Zhuangzi and related texts of Daoist thought, together with traditions of commentary, ritual and inner cultivation.
traditions.permissions_note: The Chinese base texts are streamed from the Chinese Text Project, which is credited on every page, beside Legge's public-domain English. Wang Bi's interlinear commentary is not included.

traditions.name: Confucianism
traditions.description: The Four Books and the Five Classics in James Legge's translations, with the later Confucian books, the Japanese Confucian tradition and early twentieth-century studies of the school.
traditions.permissions_note: Legge's translations of the Chinese Classics and of the Sacred Books of China are public domain in the United States. The Chinese text of the canon is streamed from the Chinese Text Project, credited on every page, and shown beside the translation.

traditions.name: Zoroastrianism
traditions.description: The Avesta, especially the Gathas attributed to Zarathushtra, and the later Pahlavi literature.
traditions.permissions_note: Catalogue entry only in this build. A reliable Avestan edition and a public-domain translation are under review; no text is displayed.

traditions.name: Jainism
traditions.description: The teachings of Mahavira and the Jain canon, with its disciplines of non-violence, asceticism and manifold predication.
traditions.permissions_note: Jacobi’s translations (1884 and 1895) are public domain in the United States. The complete Acaranga, Kalpa Sutra, Uttaradhyayana and Sutrakritanga are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive, with the printed page numbers removed from the scanned text; the Prakrit original is not included.

traditions.name: Shinto
traditions.description: The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, shrine traditions and the kami-centred ritual and mythic corpus of Japan.
traditions.permissions_note: Chamberlain's 1882 Kojiki and Aston's 1896 Nihongi are public domain and are streamed from Wikisource page by page; only the translation is hosted, and the classical Japanese/Chinese source text is not included.

traditions.name: Indigenous and oral traditions
traditions.description: Living oral traditions, songs, stories and ceremonial knowledge, which require community-defined access, attribution and consent.
traditions.permissions_note: No texts are imported. Many oral traditions are not public-domain 'works' in the Western copyright sense. Future contributions must follow community protocols and free, prior and informed consent.

traditions.name: Classical Greek and Roman philosophy
traditions.description: Greek and Roman philosophical literature, including Plato, Aristotle, the Stoics, Epicureans and Neoplatonists.
traditions.permissions_note: Jowett's Plato and Long's Marcus Aurelius are public-domain translations. Greek originals for these excerpts are not yet included.

traditions.name: Bahá’í Faith
traditions.description: The teachings of Bahá’u’lláh, the Báb and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, with authorised interpretations and the guidance of the Universal House of Justice. The tradition emphasises the unity of religions, humanity and justice.
traditions.permissions_note: The writings of Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá are streamed from the official Bahá’í Reference Library under the Community's legal terms, with its copyright notice and the work's title shown beside every chapter. They are the Community's copyright, are not relicensed, and are not used commercially. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-26.

traditions.name: Quakerism / Religious Society of Friends
traditions.description: A family of Friends’ traditions rooted in the seventeenth-century teaching of George Fox, emphasising direct experience of the Spirit, silence, equality, simplicity, integrity and peace. Theology and practice differ among yearly meetings.
traditions.permissions_note: Quaker Faith & Practice is a copyrighted book of discipline and its extracts carry separate rights; it is not imported. George Fox’s Journal (1901 Penney edition) is public domain in the United States and is included as a tested Project Gutenberg import. Other Quaker bodies maintain their own disciplines.

traditions.name: Unitarian Universalism
traditions.description: A pluralistic living tradition formed by the 1961 merger of Unitarianism and Universalism. It has no single canon and draws on multiple religious, humanist, Earth-centred and prophetic sources.
traditions.permissions_note: UUA worship and statement texts are copyrighted and their worship permission is limited to UUA member congregations. Catalogue records identify the statement and date and link to the official page; no UUA text is imported.

traditions.name: Unitarianism (historical)
traditions.description: Historical traditions that rejected Trinitarian doctrine and emphasised human moral capacity, reason and the unity of God. Distinct from, though a predecessor of, contemporary Unitarian Universalism.
traditions.permissions_note: Many nineteenth-century Unitarian sermons and treatises are public domain, but each edition must be verified. Catalogue records only in this build.

traditions.name: Universalism (historical)
traditions.description: Historical Christian traditions teaching universal salvation and the eventual restoration of all souls. A predecessor of contemporary Unitarian Universalism, with its own institutions and theologians.
traditions.permissions_note: Public-domain works exist, but no verified text is imported in this build. Catalogue records only.

traditions.name: Ethical Culture
traditions.description: A humanist religious movement founded by Felix Adler in 1876, centred on ethical relationships, social justice and the worth of every person without supernatural doctrine.
traditions.permissions_note: Movement statements and modern publications are generally copyrighted. No text is imported; catalogue metadata records the movement without treating it as a canon.

traditions.name: Humanism
traditions.description: A broad family of non-theistic ethical and philosophical stances, including organised humanist movements and secular philosophies. Not all humanism is religious, and not all secular philosophy is humanism.
traditions.permissions_note: Humanist manifestos have their own publication histories and rights. No text is imported in this build.

traditions.name: Modern Paganism
traditions.description: Contemporary religious movements drawing on pre-Christian European and other traditions, including Wicca, Druidry, Heathenry and reconstructed traditions. Modern compositions must not be presented as ancient texts.
traditions.permissions_note: Most contemporary Pagan liturgy and course material is authored and rights-managed. No text is imported. Public declarations may be catalogued and linked; closed or members-only material is respected.

traditions.name: Wicca
traditions.description: A modern initiatory Pagan religion emerging in mid-twentieth-century Britain and later diversifying into many lineages. Its texts are modern compositions, not survivals of an ancient scripture.
traditions.permissions_note: Modern Wiccan texts, including the Charge of the Goddess, are under copyright. Catalogue only; no text is reproduced.

traditions.name: Druidry
traditions.description: Modern Druid orders and fellowships inspired by ancient Celtic imagery and later revivals. Ancient druids left no scripture; modern orders have their own liturgies and training materials.
traditions.permissions_note: Modern order material is authored and often members-only. No text is imported. The registry records OBOD, ADF and related bodies for discovery.

traditions.name: Rastafari
traditions.description: A diverse Caribbean-rooted movement arising in the 1930s, centred on the divinity of Haile Selassie I, Ethiopian identity, liberation, biblical interpretation and livity. There is no single governing authority or canon.
traditions.permissions_note: Community and scholarly sources are mixed and often copyrighted. No text is imported; no single text is treated as representing all Rastafari.

traditions.name: Latter-day Saints and Restorationist traditions
traditions.description: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and related Restorationist movements, with distinct scriptures including the Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price. Other Restorationist bodies are not interchangeable with the LDS Church.
traditions.permissions_note: Official LDS scripture pages permit personal noncommercial reading and printing but prohibit posting or automated copying without permission. Catalogue only; no text is imported.

traditions.name: Tenrikyo
traditions.description: A Japanese new religious movement founded through Nakayama Miki in the nineteenth century, centring on the Ofudesaki, the service and the teaching of joyous life.
traditions.permissions_note: Official English translations are separately published and no open licence was found. Catalogue only; no text is imported.

traditions.name: Cao Dai
traditions.description: A Vietnamese syncretic religion founded in 1926, combining elements of Buddhism, Confucianism, Daoism, Christianity and local spirituality. Branches differ in organisation and authority.
traditions.permissions_note: Institutional sources exist, but the English Phap Chanh Truyen translation on the Sacerdotal Council site is explicitly not an official translation and rights are unclear. Catalogue only.

traditions.name: Theosophy
traditions.description: A modern esoteric movement associated with Helena Petrovna Blavatsky and the Theosophical Society, drawing on comparative religion, philosophy and occult claims. It has multiple organisations and no single authority.
traditions.permissions_note: Some original works are public domain, but editions, compilations and translations vary. Catalogue only in this build.

traditions.name: Anthroposophy
traditions.description: A spiritual-philosophical movement founded by Rudolf Steiner, with its own methods of knowledge, education, agriculture and the arts. It is not a single canon religion.
traditions.permissions_note: Translations and lecture transcripts carry varying rights. Catalogue only in this build.

traditions.name: Spiritualism
traditions.description: Modern traditions centred on communication with spirits, mediumship and the continuity of consciousness. Organisations and practices vary widely.
traditions.permissions_note: Historical works may be public domain, but no verified edition is imported in this build. Catalogue only.

traditions.name: Eckankar
traditions.description: A modern American spiritual movement founded by Paul Twitchell, teaching soul travel, divine sound and the Mahanta lineage. Its current organisation is the Eckankar faith.
traditions.permissions_note: Modern publications are copyrighted. Catalogue only; no text is imported.

traditions.name: Unification movement
traditions.description: The Family Federation for World Peace and Unification and related movements founded by Sun Myung Moon, with the Divine Principle as a central teaching text. The movement has split into multiple bodies.
traditions.permissions_note: Modern translations are copyrighted. Catalogue only; no text is imported.

traditions.name: Seicho-no-Ie
traditions.description: A Japanese new religious movement founded by Masaharu Taniguchi, teaching the immanence of God, the true image of humanity and gratitude-based practice.
traditions.permissions_note: Official publications and translations are copyrighted. Catalogue only.

traditions.name: Oomoto
traditions.description: A Japanese new religious movement founded through Nao Deguchi and organised by Onisaburō Deguchi, combining Shinto, esoteric and world-renewal themes.
traditions.permissions_note: Official texts and translations vary in rights. Catalogue only.

traditions.name: World Messianity / Sekai Kyusei Kyo
traditions.description: A Japanese new religious movement founded by Mokichi Okada, teaching purification, natural farming and the realisation of a paradisiacal world.
traditions.permissions_note: Modern publications are copyrighted. Catalogue only.

traditions.name: Chinese classics
traditions.description: The wider Chinese corpus beyond the Confucian and Daoist canons: the dynastic histories, the poetry and prose collections, medicine, mathematics and the encyclopedias, as the Chinese Text Project transcribes them.
traditions.permissions_note: The pre-modern Chinese text is out of copyright. The transcriptions, punctuation and apparatus the Chinese Text Project publishes are its own editorial work, credited on every page and not relicensed here.

schools.name: Śvetāmbara

schools.name: Shinto

schools.name: Stoicism

schools.name: Platonism
schools.description: The philosophical tradition stemming from Plato and the Academy.

schools.name: Britain Yearly Meeting

schools.description: The North American association of Unitarian Universalist congregations.

schools.name: Wiccan lineages

schools.description: The largest Latter-day Saint denomination.

schools.name: Spiritualist organisations
schools.description: A range of Spiritualist churches and associations.

schools.name: Seicho-no-Ie
schools.description: The movement founded by Masaharu Taniguchi.

schools.name: Oomoto
schools.description: The Oomoto movement.

schools.name: Sekai Kyusei Kyo
schools.description: The World Messianity movement.

schools.name: Sunni tradition
schools.description: The Sunni tradition, including the four classical legal schools and the hadith collections it receives as canonical.

schools.name: Shafi'i school
schools.description: The legal school of al-Shafi'i, formative for the methodology of Islamic jurisprudence.

schools.name: Hanafi school
schools.description: The legal school of Abu Hanifa, historically the most widely followed in South and Central Asia.

schools.name: Maliki school
schools.description: The legal school of Medina, founded on the practice of the city as recorded by Malik ibn Anas.

schools.name: Hanbali school
schools.description: The legal school of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, associated with a strict reliance on transmitted reports.

schools.name: Sufism
schools.description: The inward or mystical current in Islam: the practice of remembrance, the purification of the soul and the claim to direct knowledge.

schools.name: Kalam
schools.description: Rational theology in Islam, arguing the doctrines of the faith by reasoned demonstration and dialectic.

schools.name: Falsafa
schools.description: The Arabic philosophical tradition that received and transformed Greek logic, physics and metaphysics.

schools.name: Vedanta
schools.description: The schools that read the Upanishads and the Brahma Sutras as a single teaching, including Advaita, Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita.

schools.name: Yoga
schools.description: The school of Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, which sets out the discipline of stilling the mind and the stages of meditative absorption.

schools.name: Samkhya
schools.description: The dualist school of purusha and prakriti, whose analysis of consciousness and material nature underlies much of later Indian thought.

schools.name: Vaisheshika
schools.description: The school of Kanada, which classifies reality into categories and builds an atomist account of the material world.

schools.name: Mimamsa
schools.description: The school of Vedic interpretation founded on Jaimini's sutras, concerned with ritual, injunction and the authority of the revealed text.

schools.name: Vyakarana
schools.description: The grammatical tradition that begins with Panini's Astadhyayi and treats language as both a discipline and a route to understanding.

schools.name: Jyotisha
schools.description: The astronomical and astrological tradition, including the siddhantas on the motions of the sun, moon and planets.

schools.name: Shaivism
schools.description: The traditions that worship Shiva as the supreme principle, including the tantric schools of Kashmir and the Shaiva Puranas.

schools.name: Shaktism
schools.description: The traditions centred on the Goddess, her power and her mantra and tantric worship.

schools.name: Puranic tradition
schools.description: The encyclopaedic Puranic literature, whose sectarian allegiances range across Vishnu, Shiva and the Goddess within a single work.

schools.name: Twelver Shi'ism
schools.description: The Twelver Shia tradition, its hadith collections, law and theology, including the school of the Imams and its later jurists.

schools.name: Maturidi
schools.description: The Sunni school of kalam founded by Abu Mansur al-Maturidi, which reads revelation through a rational defence of God's unity and attributes.

schools.name: Mu'tazili
schools.description: The school of kalam that argued for the unity and justice of God, the createdness of the Qur'an and the primacy of reason in theology.

schools.name: Nyaya
schools.description: The school of logic, debate and epistemology, whose sutras are attributed to Gautama and whose oldest commentary is that of Vatsyayana.

schools.name: Zahiri
schools.description: The literalist school of law, which derives rulings from the plain sense of the Qur'an and hadith and rejects analogy; its chief surviving exponent is Ibn Hazm.

authors.name: Anselm of Canterbury

authors.name: Thomas Aquinas

authors.name: Aryabhata
authors.description: Astronomer and mathematician of Kusumapura, author of the Aryabhatiya, whose rules for planetary motion, sines and place-value arithmetic shaped Indian astronomy.

authors.name: Aryasura
authors.description: Buddhist poet of the Sanskrit tradition, author of the Jātakamālā, the retelling of the Buddha's former births in classical verse and prose.

authors.name: Ashtavakra
authors.description: The sage of the Mahabharata, bent in eight places in his mother's womb, whose dialogue with king Janaka is preserved as the Ashtavakra Gita.

authors.name: Aśvaghoṣa
authors.description: Sanskrit poet and dramatist of the early Kuṣāṇa period, author of the Buddhacarita, the earliest complete life of the Buddha in classical Sanskrit.

authors.name: Athanasius of Alexandria
authors.description: Bishop of Alexandria and defender of the Nicene formula against Arius and his successors.

authors.name: Farid al-Din Attar
authors.description: Persian poet and Sufi, author of the Conference of the Birds and the Memorial of the Saints.

authors.name: Augustine of Hippo
authors.description: Bishop of Hippo and one of the most influential Latin theologians; author of the Confessions, The City of God and On Christian Doctrine.

authors.name: The Báb
authors.description: Founder of the Bábí movement and a central figure for Bahá’ís.

sources.name: GRETIL

sources.description: A register of Sanskrit, Pali and Prakrit e-texts, each transcribed by a named scholar from a stated printed edition, with an analytic HTML transformation and a plain-text transformation of every file.
sources.access_notes: Each work is streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time, with a descriptive user agent; the import cache holds the validated segments so the register is never crawled twice. sources.name: Internet Sacred Text Archive
sources.description: Public-domain translations of scripture and commentary, served as one HTML page per chapter or sutra section. sources.access_notes: Chapter-sized pages are fetched once when a reader opens them and held in the stream cache; the importers keep the validated segments so the host is not crawled again. Requests carry a descriptive user agent. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-22; the old pages are read from archive.sacred-texts.com because the site's current interface blocks scripted clients.

sources.name: Gita Supersite / Heritage IIT Kanpur
sources.description: The Bhagavad Gita in Sanskrit, verse by verse, with the Sanskrit commentaries the platform publishes — the bhashyas of Shankara, Ramanuja, Madhva, Abhinavagupta and the rest — in the script the reader chooses.
sources.access_notes: One chapter of the Sanskrit moolam and of the Sanskrit commentaries is streamed from heritage.iitk.ac.in at read time. Only the Tier A and Tier B content of HCAL 1.1 is imported; the modern translations and commentaries of Tier C are not. Access was authorised by the project owner on 2026-10-26.
